import html # Example invitation format; in a real application this would be defined elsewhere. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
{additional_notes}
""" def generate_event_invite(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a secure HTML invitation. Parameters ---------- title : str The event's title or name. description : str Detailed description of the event. May contain multiple paragraphs. date : str Scheduled date of the event. notes : str Supplementary information or instructions. Returns ------- str A sanitized HTML string suitable for safe rendering in a browser. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is empty or not a string. """ # Basic type and emptiness checks for name, value in (("title", title), ("description", description), ("date", date), ("notes", notes)): if not isinstance(value, str): raise ValueError(f"{name!r} must be a string") if not value.strip(): raise ValueError(f"{name!r} cannot be empty") # Escape user-provided content to prevent XSS escaped = { "event_title": html.escape(title, quote=True), "event_description": html.escape(description, quote=False).replace("\n", "
"), "event_date": html.escape(date, quote=True), "additional_notes": html.escape(notes, quote=False).replace("\n", "
"), } # Render the template with sanitized values return INVITATION_FORMAT.format(**escaped)
